Issue_Reported: A blood overdraw of 1 ml occurred during PE/Nitroprusside testing. During the first blood draw, a faulty vacutainer resulted in obtaining only 1 ml of blood. The ~1 ml blood drawn in the faulty vacutainer was discarded. Instead of the nominal 27 mL blood draw, the total amount drawn for testing was 28 ml.
Description_of_Action_Taken: The blood draw was instead completed by syringe. The blood draw using a syringe did NOT require an additional needle stick. The overdraw occurred due to a materials failure. The vacutainer did not draw the amount of blood for which it was designed. It pulled roughly 1 ml of blood, the amount of the overdraw. Occasionally, a faulty vacutainer with an inadequate vacuum will draw less than the amount that it is supposed to draw. When this occurs, the blood in the failed tube cannot be used for the purpose of the test because the quantity of preservative in the tube is specific for a particular volume. Removing the tube top and adding blood is not practical because the resulting volume may still be inaccurate. Issue reported by Chris Ribeiro, cardiovascular team.
